implemented: Migration 101 adds one pending, expiring ownership request per application with sender, recipient and application foreign keys.
Only the current human owner can address a request to another live human account. Expired requests are removed before a replacement is created.
Only the named recipient can accept or decline. Acceptance atomically changes the owner, revokes every old credential, creates one replacement credential hash, and removes outstanding requests.
The replacement plaintext token is returned once after commit and the bot runtime is disconnected after durable rotation.
The TR/EN application settings panel can send requests, list incoming requests, accept or decline, and exposes the rotated token in the existing transient one-time-token surface.
OpenAPI and the route golden include all three transfer endpoints.
checks: Service integration proves a stranger cannot accept, the named recipient can accept, the old token becomes invalid, the new token authenticates, ownership moves, and runtime disconnect occurs.
Handler tests prove bot identities cannot manage transfers and acceptance returns the rotated credential.
Full Go test ./... passed after migration and route changes.
Full client Vitest passed 180 files and 1875 tests; TypeScript project checking passed.
